text: Every RCM row cites at least one clause that exists in the loaded regulatory corpus.
A finding is released only with triple citation (regulatory clause, control, evidence reference); otherwise it is blocked.
A finding may not cite a clause outside the grounding set retrieved for it, or a clause absent from the corpus.
A test conclusion of Effective cannot stand when exceptions were recorded.
A test conclusion of Effective requires at least one evidence reference.
Every module execution and human action writes an audit-trail bundle with inputs, retrieval set, execution log, QA actions, output, actor and versions.
The audit trail is tamper-evident: any change to a past bundle is detected by chain verification.
Findings require review by a reviewer, then approval by a different approver; each sign-off records name, role, meaning and time.
Approved findings are locked against edit and regeneration.
The audit report includes approved findings only; others are listed as excluded.
Modules run only in chain order (scope, RCM, testing, gaps, report).
Content packs are schema-validated on load; a control citing an unknown clause is rejected.
Retrieval returns the expert-expected clauses for labelled queries.
Model output is constrained: controls outside the library are rejected, and a failed model call falls back to deterministic rules with a QA flag.
Actions are restricted by role (auditor, audit manager, CAE, admin, viewer); admins and viewers cannot change audit work.
Users authenticate through the configured OIDC identity provider; demo sign-in is impossible in production (21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(d)).

Trail records cannot be updated, deleted or truncated, and approved findings cannot be changed, at the database level (21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(e), ALCOA+). Enforced against the application's code paths; separating the API's database role from the owner role is delivered in plan 1F.

Concurrent conflicting edits are never silently overwritten at the API: changes serialise per engagement, a request carrying If-Match with a stale version is rejected (409 VERSION_CONFLICT), and state and its trail entries commit or roll back together. (UI use of If-Match: plan 1B.)
Knowledge retrieval never returns content the requesting user may not access: classification by role, engagement scope and retention are enforced inside the database query.
Actions are authorised by role, and the preparer, reviewer and approver of a finding are distinct people (21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(g)).
Signing requires re-authentication within 120 seconds, bound to a single-use signing request for that finding, meaning and content (21 CFR Part 11 §11.200(a)).
Each signature records full name, meaning and time, is displayed with the record, and is bound to the signed content by hash (21 CFR Part 11 §11.50, §11.70).
Only human-verified, active, non-stale knowledge nodes are citable in released outputs; unverified sources block release unless explicitly allowed outside production, and stale sources are flagged.
`verify` detects trail, signature or stored-document tampering after restore.
Configuration is validated at start-up; insecure combinations are refused.
The agent can only take actions the engagement graph allows from the current state; no model output can skip a gate.
Gates are closed only by a human Part 11 signature bound to the subject's content; the agent never signs, records test results or edits reviewed findings.
Every agent decision is typed, attributed to the agent on behalf of its starter, and recorded in the hash-chained trail.
Runs stop at their budget, and the kill switch prevents new agent work.
Every workpaper is reviewed by the QA agent before its gate opens, and the review is shown to the signer.
Every judgment the agent makes is recorded with its basis and rationale in a memo that is part of the subject the signer approves.

Offline, every judgment is a deterministic rule; a model may only tighten a judgment (raise a risk, worsen a severity or an opinion, add an issue), never relax one. Only a person relaxes one, and each relaxation is trailed and named in the memo.
A test conclusion accepts exceptions only within a tolerance a person set for that control, recorded outside the signed workpapers; the agent never sets a tolerance.
Management responses are recorded outside signed finding content; recording one never alters a signed finding or breaks its signature.
The engagement context is written only by people, and a change to it after the scope gate reopens the scope.

The assistant runs only catalogued commands as the signed-in person: reads carry that person's permissions, every write needs their explicit confirmation and is trailed as their own action, and no command signs, approves or rejects anything.

Text the assistant retrieves or is shown (documents, engagement names, finding titles, earlier turns) reaches its model only as delimited data, and cannot make it run a command the person did not confirm.
Extracted text and chunks derive only from the stored bytes identified by sha256, with the extractor and its version recorded; every document has an extraction status.
